tagline.text: A calm island off San Carlos, quiet beaches you can circle in a day by motorbike

location.label: Location
location.text: Off San Carlos City, Negros Occidental (barangays San Juan and Ermita)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (transport, lodging and food, rough estimate per person for 1 night)

children.text: Sipaway Island lies just in front of San Carlos harbor and is also called Refugio Island. A pumpboat gets you there in about 15 minutes, you can ride around the whole island in a day by motorbike, and it is known for white sand beaches, a century-old balete tree and quiet resorts.

Sipaway Island is an island off San Carlos City in Negros Occidental. It is also known as Refugio Island (the Coast Guard lighthouse on it is listed as Refugio Island Light), and Wikipedia says it shelters San Carlos's natural harbor from bad weather, though no other source states this. The island is made up of two barangays, Ermita and San Juan, and measures about
7 km
from one end to the other. That is why you can go all the way around it in a day by motorcycle taxi or tricycle. Local bangkas and pumpboats connect it with the mainland. The island is only about
1.5 km

wide, so the sea is close wherever you are. Reports from 2018 and 2021 describe a quiet community with many empty lots and few houses, and say that the arrival of electricity and water was a big change.

The atmosphere is very different from a resort island like Boracay. Visitor accounts say there are no bars or nightlife and that life moves slowly. They say the sand is not as powdery as Boracay's but is beautiful and less developed, comparable to the beaches of Guimaras. At some beaches you need high tide to swim well, while at low tide the sand flats are exposed over a wide area, so check the tides when you plan your day. Some stretches of coast still have mangroves, though there are also reports of them being rehabilitated after typhoon damage.

The island's best-known sight is an old balete tree on the grounds of San Juan Elementary School. Locals sometimes call it Lunok, and one visitor says its canopy is broad but the tree is not as tall as expected. Other places that come up repeatedly in accounts are Crystal Beach, Parana Beach (also called North Blue Beach) and Whispering Palms Island Resort. Much of this information comes from blog posts from around 2014, so fees and whether places are open may differ now. Ask your lodging or boatman before you go. Visitors also mention La Basilia White Beach Resort on the Ermita side, and one chartered a pumpboat by asking the boatman to drop them in front of that resort.
San Carlos is a city on the east coast of Negros Occidental, about
87 km
from Bacolod by road and about
2 hours

by bus. Its port has RORO service to Toledo in Cebu, so it is used as a crossing between Bacolod and Cebu. Sipaway is the city's front-yard island, so it pairs well with a 2-day, 1-night trip. Every year on November 3–5 San Carlos holds the Pintaflores Festival, so if you come then you can see the city's event as well.
From the San Carlos pier, a pumpboat reaches the island in about
10–15 minutes
. Travel guides from 2023–2024 give the fare as ₱15, and older accounts say ₱10–15. Tell the boatman the name of your resort and he will drop you at the nearest wharf.

A tree described as a balete (a strangler fig) more than 100 years old, on the grounds of San Juan Elementary School. Its canopy spreads wide, which makes for good photos. It is on school grounds, so visit quietly during class hours.
A quiet, unfenced beach with no benches and just a few huts. A 2014 account says the caretaker asked ₱20 per person for upkeep, and it is described as good for swimming.
A privately run beach with a fenced swimming area for high tide. In 2014 the entrance fee was reported as ₱20.

Described as the most modern resort on the island, with its own power generation. A 2023 guide lists rooms from ₱2,500 and 2026 booking sites show about ₱2,200–3,500, while older accounts' ₱1,350–3,500 is out of date. Its beach also sells day passes that include lunch.

The island is small, so you can hire a motorcycle taxi for half a day and see it all. Accounts mention about ₱200, but no recent figure confirms it (short tricycle or motorbike hops on the island are reported at ₱15–25) and there is no fixed rate, so negotiate at the wharf.
A dive operator called Sipaway Dives is said to start from the Whispering Palms beach. If you want to dive, book ahead and check equipment and schedule with the operator.

A 2021 guide lists swimming in clear water and snorkeling, plus camping on the beach with a bonfire and stargazing, among the things to do. Camping may need the beach owner's permission, so ask your lodging or the village first.

items.subtitle: Beach walks and sunset after arrival

children.text: Take a Ceres bus from Bacolod to San Carlos. The route through Don Salvador Benedicto is described as about
2 hours
and the coastal road as about
3.5 hours
From the San Carlos terminal, take a tricycle to the pier and have lunch.
Cross to the island by pumpboat and check in to your lodging.
Swim at the beach or rent a motorbike to see the island. Swimming is best at high tide.
Walk the beach at sunset. Some small resorts have power only in the evening, so bring a light for after dark.
There is no nightlife on the island. Plan a quiet, restful stay.

items.title: The next day
items.subtitle: The balete tree and one more beach

children.text: After breakfast, take a motorcycle taxi to see the San Juan balete tree, Crystal Beach and more.
Spend the rest of the time relaxing at a beach you like.
Return to San Carlos by pumpboat, then continue by bus to Bacolod or by ferry to Toledo.
Check the last bus and ferry times to Bacolod and Cebu in advance. If you have time, you can see the cathedral and old houses in San Carlos town.
There are domestic flights from Manila to Bacolod-Silay Airport (BCD). Check flight times and fares on the airline's website for your dates.
From the airport, travel to the city terminal by taxi or van.
Ceres buses run from Bacolod to San Carlos. The route through Don Salvador Benedicto is described as about
2 hours
and the coastal road as about
3.5 hours
The distance by road is about
87 km
. Accounts give the fare as roughly ₱100 and up.
Take a bus from Cebu to Toledo, then a RORO ferry or fastcraft from Toledo to San Carlos. One account says the fastcraft takes about
35 minutes
Check schedules and fares with the ferry company.
From San Carlos town, take a tricycle to the pier and board a pumpboat. It takes about
10–15 minutes
, and guides from 2023–2024 give the fare as about ₱15, and older accounts say ₱10–15.
Some boats leave when full while others run at set intervals, according to accounts, so check the schedule locally.
Chartering a boat is reported at about ₱190, but this may change.
The dry season, November to May, has calmer seas and more reliable beach days. In the rainy season the waves get rough and boat trips can be disrupted.
Tides matter if you want to swim on the island. Swimming is best at high tide, and at low tide the sand flats are exposed over a wide area. Ask your lodging for that day's high tide time.

rows: Calm seas, good for beach plans
The midday sun is strong, so be active in the morning and evening
Boats may be delayed, and avoid typhoon season

There are no large hotels on the island, only small resorts and homestays. Whispering Palms is described as the most modern and as using its own power. Some small resorts have electricity only in the evening (about 17:30 to 23:30 in one account), so check with your lodging. The tap water is said to be supplied from San Carlos.

Accounts describe the island's evenings as quiet. Some say resort staff will cook for you, but it is safer to bring your own water and snacks. It is easiest to prepare what you need in San Carlos town before you cross.

A 2021 guide warns that on some resorts electricity runs for only a few hours each night and that water can run short in summer. It says power and water have been on around the clock for a few years, but this differs by lodging, so check when you book. Whispering Palms is said to take inquiries through its Facebook page or website.
Time your swim for high tide. Ask your lodging about the tides.
Carry plenty of cash. I could not confirm whether the island has an ATM, so withdraw cash in San Carlos beforehand.
Charge your phone during the day. Some lodgings have power only in the evening.
Tell the boatman your resort's name and he will drop you at the nearest wharf.
Accounts also advise bringing extra food and bottled water, so pack water and snacks.
Motorcycle taxis have no fixed rate, so agree on the price before you ride.
Some beaches are private, so a fee or permission may be required.
Check the last bus times to Bacolod and Cebu in advance.
If you come by car, find a place to park near the pier first. Guides say you can enter Sipaway Island in your navigation app, but check parking locally.
Accounts say that if you ask a motorcycle taxi driver to take you to the balete tree, it is well known to locals and easy to find.
Facilities on the island are basic, with limited power and eating options, and boats can stop during the rainy season and typhoons, so check the weather.
The fees and entry details here come from blog accounts dating from 2014 to recent years and may differ now.
Some beaches are hard to swim at low tide, so plan around high tide.
Parts of a beach may still be under repair after typhoon damage, so ask your lodging before you visit.
Do not step on or break off corals and mangroves.
Avoid moving around at night and reach your lodging before dark.
A 2021 guide lists the Broce Ancestral House, the Hacienda Sta. Ana Grotto and the San Carlos Borromeo Cathedral as sights in town. You can see them before or after the crossing.
A beach resort on the southwest coast of Negros Occidental, good to continue to as another beach destination in the same province.
The provincial capital about
2 hours
away by road, and the hub for flights and buses.
A coral reef in the Sagay Marine Reserve in northern Negros Occidental. It needs a separate day.
